headline: City Council passed a gas leaf blower ban that excludes City and DPS work, and September minutes were approved.
summary: Kyle Davis, the council liaison, gave updates on a native planting ordinance and a rooftop wind ordinance. Members also heard about the new PowerChoice contract, which now offers only Basic and Plus, and about the Energy Fair on Nov. 9.
decisions: Approved the Sept. 23, 2026 regular meeting minutes 4-0.
City Council passed a gas leaf blower ban, with City and DPS not included.

98 WASHINGTON STREET, SALEM, MASSACHUSETTS 01970 ♦ TEL: 978.745.9595 FAX: 978.740.0404 ♦  WWW.SALEMMA.GOV

MINUTES
Present: John Hayes, Will Winn, Kevin Rice, Leigh Chander, Bill Burnham
Absent: Zach Calderon (resigning)
Introductions 
City Council Liaison Update (Kyle Davis)
 Gas leaf blower ban passed at City Council meeting before the last one. All Councilors 
were on board but got stuck on specifics re seasonal bans, how many years out until 
enforcement (2030), etc., with the biggest debate revolving around whether the 
City/DPS should be included. The City/DPS will NOT be included, but the issue will be 
revisited in a few years as technology improves.
 Conversations continue regarding the Native Planting Ordinance. We are on the right 
path, but this would codify City practice, and we would love to see a certain percentage 
of native plants required for developers.
o John Hayes wonders if Salem's changing climate was considered (milder, warmer 
winters). How can the Ordinance change with global warming? This has not been 
discussed. 
o The City’s Municipal Vulnerability Assessment from December 2014 is discussed
 Will Winn asks about the residential wind ordinance.
o A joint meeting with the City Council and Planning Board was held; wind energy 
systems look like small wind turbines (minutes and recording not yet available)
o Will be on next Council Agenda, but Planning Board was supportive
o Unknown: how readily can people adopt this technology
o Put link to the City Council meeting where this was discussed on social media 
when available, not on SERC website
o Stacy to send Battery Storage ordinance link to SERC (not yet at that stage; 
holding off)
